sources.cite: Microsoft Learn (Azure Pipelines), Define approvals and checks
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-18. 'Before the execution of a stage can begin, all checks on all the resources used in that stage must be satisfied'; checks can be set on environments, service connections, repositories, variable groups, secure files and agent pools; 'a manual approval check on an environment ensures that deployment to that environment only happens after the designated user reviews the changes'; 'Approvals and other checks aren't defined in the yaml file.' That a stage which deploys through the service connection without targeting the environment does not consume it, so the environment's approval never runs, is the author's reading (a stage only waits for checks on resources it uses).

brief.situation: You are the DevOps engineer at Norland Payments. Production deployments must be approved by a release manager through the 'production' environment's approval check. The auditor found that last night's change reached production with no approval recorded. Your pipeline review with the auditor is at 16:00, and the same pipeline must ship a fee-calculation hotfix today, approved.
handover: The 'production' environment has an approval check: release-managers group, one approver.
Last month the deploy stage was rewritten to call a shared deployment template.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the pipeline's prod stage, the production environment and its approval check, and the service connection the stage deploys with.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why approvals were skipped, what you changed, and how the control holds for every path.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: Since the rewrite the Prod stage was a plain job calling a template that deploys with sc-prod; it never used the production environment, and a stage only waits for checks on resources it uses.

parts.label: Changed
parts.modelAnswer: Made Prod a deployment job targeting environment production in both pipelines; the hotfix run waited for and recorded the release manager's approval. A laptop deploy repeats the gap; more approvers on an unused environment change nothing.

parts.label: Every path
parts.modelAnswer: The same approval is on the sc-prod service connection, and the environment requires the approved template.

findingOpen.headline: Checks apply to the resources a stage uses

approved.body: You read the stage and the run history, saw the environment was never targeted, made the job a deployment job in both pipelines, shipped the hotfix with a recorded approval, and put a check on the credentials themselves.

scoring.modelReasoning: The approval exists on the environment, but the run history shows no stage has used the environment since the rewrite: Prod is a plain job deploying through the service connection. Checks run for resources a stage consumes, so make Prod a deployment job targeting the production environment in both pipelines and ship the hotfix through it, checking the approval is recorded. Deploying by hand repeats the finding; more approvers on an unused environment change nothing. Then put the approval on the service connection too.
